messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — elevated paging to KV cache daemon group. Rate of cache eviction has spiked, sustained page-in from NVMe for 8m. Top affected route: /v2/generate (model: rwd-7b-opt).

ryan_h: ack, I'm on it. seeing a 4x tail latency increase on eu-west nodes. starting triage.

naomi_s: I'm tailing logs and seeing repeated NCCL warnings around ring timeout on gpu-tp-1-*. Could be TP shard imbalance + huge kv entries triggering cross-gpu transfers.

marcus_g: +1 on NCCL. stack traces show frequent queue-full/backpressure on the KV flush path. Also noticing continuous-batching spikes — batch sizes jump to >1024 tokens when prefix cache miss happens.

devon_w: any recent deploys? I see a config change 2h ago bumping continuous_batch.max_tokens to 2000 in prod. Reverting would be fastest mitigation.

ryan_h: rollback suggested. prepping a hotpatch to drop continuous_batch.max_tokens to 256 and force-disable continuous_batching for the KV-heavy routes.

emily_p: tagging SRE for possible rolling restart plan if NCCL stalls persist after config change: @oncall.

ops_tooling_bot: Runbook matched: KV_CACHE_PAGING_INCIDENT v2. Suggested mitigations: 1) reduce batch size, 2) enable aggressive kv-eviction, 3) rebalance tp shards if NCCL errors continue.

naomi_s: pasting error snippet from gpu node (sanitized):

```
[W NCCL] Unhandled error, NCCL operation timed out
[ERR kv.c:142] shard_index mismatch: expected 3 got 1
[INFO memory] fallback to NVMe paging for big kv item id=0x7f3a
```

marcus_g: that shard_index mismatch is the smoking gun. Some KV entries ended up assigned to the wrong TP partition after the last rolling update to the shard map. Combined with bigger batches it's forcing huge NCCL cross-talk.

ryan_h: deploying hotpatch now: commit https://github.com/redwood/runtime/commit/4f9b12a — changes: continuous_batch.max_tokens=256, continuous_batch.enabled=false, kv.cache_limit_bytes=64424509440 (60GB), kv.evict_policy=lrucapped.

devon_w: apply rollout to eu-west cluster only, 2 nodes at a time to avoid global blast. I'll handle canaries.

ops_tooling_bot: Deploy started: runtime/hotfix/4f9b12a -> prod-eu-west. Canary nodes: gpu-tp-1-3, gpu-tp-1-4.

naomi_s: monitoring NCCL logs and kv paging metrics. initial canary shows paging drops ~70% and tail latency down ~35% on those nodes.

marcus_g: good. but still seeing 1-2 nodes with persistent NCCL ring timeout errors — likely the shard_map is still inconsistent. We should run the shard reassign script to revalidate partition checksums and reassign missing ranges.

ryan_h: agreed. running kv_shard_reassign.sh in dry-run first.

```
# dry-run
./tools/kv_shard_reassign.sh --cluster eu-west --dry-run --report /tmp/shard-reassign-1775554321.json
```

emily_p: output looks safe. Proposed plan: 1) dry-run -> 2) run reassign on one affected node group -> 3) restart worker process on that node only -> 4) observe for 10m.

devon_w: doing step 2 now on gpu-tp-1-6 (least load). running with throttle to avoid big NCCL churn.

ops_tooling_bot: Shard reassign started for node gpu-tp-1-6. Changes planned: move kv ranges [1200-1248] from shard 1 -> shard 3.

naomi_s: after reassign, that node's NCCL errors cleared. paging went down and NVMe read rate dropped to baseline.

ryan_h: rolling the reassign + single-worker restarts across the remaining affected group (one node at a time). tracking 95th latency and paging IOPS.

marcus_g: customer impact summary so far: ~12 customers saw request latency > 10s for a short window; 3 customers reported timeouts and 429s during peak. No data loss, only transient degraded latency.

emily_p: created incident ticket INC-2026-4589 and notified Account Mgmt for the three impacted customers.

ryan_h: final metrics after full rollout & reassign: paging down 88% cluster-wide, 95th latency back within SLOs. NCCL errors dropped to normal noise levels.

naomi_s: logs show a small number of KV items with unusually large size (~1.2GB) which amplified the problem when they were placed on wrong shard. Adding an alert for oversized-kv-items (>256MB) and auto-rejecting writes over a threshold.

marcus_g: followups (postmortem actions):
- enforce kv item size limits + validation in write path
- add shard checksum verification to cluster-start
- improve canary for config changes (auto-disable high continuous_batch values)
- add a mitigation playbook for TP shard reassigns

devon_w: rolling handoff: I'm handing oncall to @emily_p for overnight watch. all mitigation steps documented in the ticket.

emily_p: taking handoff — will watch paging and NCCL error rates for 12h. if regressions reappear, escalate to infra-leads.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by oncall team. Severity: P2. Duration ~2h 27m.

ryan_h: nice work everyone. we'll write up the full postmortem with timeline and customer comms. :trophy:
